notes:
Context: Stratus is a mid-market omni-channel retailer building a unified inference layer for product recommendations, conversational customer support, and site search reranking. They have a 100ms target for recommendation microservices (steady-state) and want clear latency/throughput guarantees for a Dedicated contract. Key ask: sizing workshop to produce baseline QPS, tokens/sec, reserved GPU plan, and SLA proposal.

Traffic profile (from pre-workshop questionnaire):
- Steady-state QPS: 80 requests/sec (recommendation microservice calling generation model for re-rank + short completion ~80-120 tokens).
- Peak (30-45 min flash sale windows): bursts up to 1,400 requests/sec across services, with heavy tail to 2,000 rps for search+chat combined.
- Token distribution: 70% short responses (<=120 tokens), 25% medium (120-512), 5% long form (>512) — mainly for agent transcripts.
- User latency expectations: P95 <= 150ms for recommendations (critical), P99 <= 400ms acceptable for chat.

Workshop objectives:
- Validate QPS and token/sec baselines via synthetic load tests and production trace sampling.
- Map each workload to candidate model families (distilled Llama variants for recs, 7-13B chat models for conversational agent).
- Derive reserved GPU counts by workload using token/sec capacity per GPU (A100/H100 profiles).
- Define autoscale/burst policy: reserved baseline capacity + pre-provisioned burst pool + cross-region fallback.
- Draft SLA clauses: latency SLOs (P95/P99), throughput guarantees (sustained QPS, short-burst allowance), maintenance windows, and credit/penalty language.

Preliminary sizing notes (from SE analysis, subject to load test confirmation):
- Recommendation microservice (distilled 7B, quantized): ~60 steady QPS could be satisfied by 2x A100 GPUs with batching (target batch sizes 8-16) assuming avg 100 tokens/req => ~6,000 tok/sec per GPU. Reserve 2 GPUs baseline per region.
- Search/rerank (embedding+rerank hybrid): embeddings handled by hosted embedters for now; rerank uses 13B model at lower QPS — expected steady 20 qps, burst to 250 qps. Plan: reserve 1-2 GPUs with pre-warmed KV cache.
- Chat/agent (13B/70B for high-quality): low steady QPS (5-10) but high token/sec during transcripts. Prefer burstable pool with autoscale to cover flash spikes; recommend 2 reserved GPUs + 4-8 burst GPUs depending on SLA.
- Peak planning: to tolerate 1,400-2,000 rps across services during sales events, recommend a mix of reserved + burst: baseline reserved 6-8 GPUs per region with an additional burst pool ability to add 12-16 GPUs for 30-60 minute spikes. Cost trade-offs to be modeled in follow-ups.

SLA negotiation points to surface during procurement:
- Define sustained throughput: how long is a "burst" (30m? 1h?) and what is allowed without penalty?
- Failover behavior: automatic fallback to smaller models / different region without violating data residency.
- Maintenance windows: max monthly downtime allowance, notification windows, and emergency patching process.
- Monitoring/observability: token-level billing, per-model latency heatmaps, and tracing for slow requests.
- Incident SLAs: MTTD and MTTR targets for production service impacting Dedicated instances.

Open questions for workshop:
- Can customer provide 48 hours of anonymized traces including token counts to run realistic replay? (they can provide 24h today).
- Preference on GPU types (H100 vs A100) — cost vs latency trade. Customer leans H100 for chat quality but cost-sensitive for recs.
- Legal: indemnity and data residency language — legal team wants draft by next procurement round.

Stubs/links: see attached drive doc (capacity-sizing-template v1), security FAQ sent, and demo recording. SE action items: prepare A100/H100 perf matrix, run synthetic load to validate tok/sec per GPU, and draft initial SLA language for review.
